plain_english: "You preach poverty but live in a mansion." Yes. I am not yet as wise as I want to be. But even if you judge me harshly, I am further along than you. That is enough for now.
original_excerpt: You tell me I do not practice what I preach. I am not yet wise. And even if I were, I would not be the wisest of men.

plain_english: Wealth is not evil. The wise person does not reject money — they just refuse to let it own them. Hold your possessions loosely. Enjoy them, but be ready to give them up without pain.
original_excerpt: The wise man does not deem himself undeserving of any of the gifts of fortune. He does not love riches but prefers them.

plain_english: The person I am trying to become is better than the person I am today. That is all I can promise. I will fall short. I will contradict myself. But I will keep going. That is what philosophy asks of you — not perfection, but persistence.
original_excerpt: I am not good. I shall never be good. I prepare not remedies for my own sores, but for yours. Yet in this I am not wholly unlike a physician who, though himself sick, tries to find cures.
